name: 3,3'-Diindolylmethane (DIM)
short: Case reports, cause not shown: leg and lung clots (65-year-old man, other risk factors); stroke (38-year-old woman, patent foramen ovale). Trial in women on tamoxifen: lower tamoxifen metabolites.
text: In randomised trials, DIM was reported as well tolerated in 551 women with low-grade cervical abnormalities (the abstract does not state the route) and, taken by mouth, in 45 men with prostate cancer before surgery; in an interim report of a trial of DIM by mouth in 64 women with cervical dysplasia, 2 participants (3%) reported nausea and no systemic toxicities were seen on blood tests. In contrast, a placebo-controlled trial of DIM given as vaginal suppositories in 78 women reported adverse events in 40-42% of those on DIM versus 22% on placebo, a statistically significant difference, with no serious adverse events. A case report described a 65-year-old man, who had other risk factors including smoking and a possible earlier pulmonary embolism, who developed deep venous thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary embolism after 3 to 4 months of DIM; the authors called this a possible association needing further study. Another case report described an ischaemic stroke in a healthy 38-year-old woman with a patent foramen ovale who was using DIM; case reports cannot show that DIM caused these events. In a 12-month placebo-controlled trial in 130 women prescribed tamoxifen, DIM by mouth reduced plasma levels of tamoxifen metabolites, including endoxifen; adverse events were minimal and did not differ between groups, and the authors said further research is needed to find out whether this reduction lessens the clinical benefit of tamoxifen.
